references.text: Pilate had already declared earlier that he found no guilt in Jesus (Luke 23:4). Now Herod confirms this by sending Jesus back without finding anything worthy of punishment.
Pilate repeats for the third time that he finds nothing deserving of death in Jesus (Luke 23:22), which underscores the same point as in verse 15: nothing deserving of death has been done by him.
Herod's interrogation of Jesus is described in Luke 23:6-12. Pilate refers to this hearing in verse 15 and notes that neither did Herod find anything worthy of the death penalty.
Similarly, Festus found that Paul had done nothing deserving of death (Acts 25:25), a parallel to Pilate's declaration of Jesus' innocence.
Agrippa and Festus concluded about Paul: 'This man has done nothing deserving of death or imprisonment' (Acts 26:31). Luke uses similar language to show the innocence of both Jesus and Paul.
The thief on the cross confirms Jesus' innocence with the words 'this man has done nothing wrong' (Luke 23:41), reflecting Pilate's and Herod's conclusion in verse 15.
Verse 14 is the immediate context where Pilate says he has interrogated Jesus without finding him guilty (Luke 23:14). Verse 15 continues by pointing out that neither did Herod find guilt.
Also in John's Gospel, Pilate declares: 'I find no fault in him' (John 18:38), a parallel declaration of innocence that aligns with the message in Luke 23:15.
Pilate repeats in John 19:4 that he finds no guilt in Jesus, confirming the same theme of Jesus' innocence that Luke highlights in 23:15.

Peter writes about Christ that 'he committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth' (1 Peter 2:22). This confirms theologically what Pilate and Herod concluded: Jesus had done nothing deserving of death.
